intent.raw_query: Edinburgh history and whisky, $2000 solo, 5 days, September 2027, from London

experiences.name: Edinburgh Castle Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic fortress perched on volcanic rock, home to the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, and the famous One O'Clock Gun. Delve into over 1,000 years of Scottish history through immersive exhibits and stunning panoramic views of the city.

experiences.name: Scotch Whisky Experience
experiences.description: Embark on a sensory journey through the world of Scotch whisky at this award-winning attraction next to the castle. Enjoy a barrel ride through the whisky-making process, guided tastings of single malts from all five whisky-producing regions of Scotland, and access to one of the world's largest Scotch whisky collections.
experiences.location: Castlehill, Royal Mile, Old Town, Edinburgh

experiences.name: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided walking tour along Edinburgh's most famous street, stretching from Edinburgh Castle to the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Discover hidden closes, medieval architecture, tales of plague, body snatchers, and the turbulent history of Mary Queen of Scots with an expert local guide.

experiences.name: Whisky Trail at the Canongate Pubs
experiences.description: Self-guided whisky crawl through some of Edinburgh's most historic and atmospheric pubs along the lower Royal Mile. Sample rare single malts and blended Scotch whiskies at legendary establishments like The Tolbooth Tavern and The Canongate, while soaking in centuries-old pub culture and local storytelling.

experiences.name: Underground Vaults & Mary King's Close Tour
experiences.description: Descend beneath the Royal Mile into the eerie, preserved 17th-century streets and chambers of Mary King's Close. Guided by costumed actors, uncover the lives of Edinburgh's plague victims, merchants, and ordinary citizens who once lived in these subterranean alleyways, offering a uniquely haunting window into the city's dark past.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Airlink 100 bus (£4.50 one-way) from the airport to Waverley Bridge in the city centre, then walk or take a short bus to your Old Town accommodation. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour — after settling in, join an afternoon guided walking tour along the Royal Mile. This stretches from Edinburgh Castle down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Many free or low-cost self-guided options exist; look for free walking tours with a tip-based model (£0–£10 suggested tip). Get your bearings, soak in the medieval architecture, and discover closes and wynds off the main street.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to Grassmarket, a historic square at the foot of Edinburgh Castle. Browse the lively pubs and enjoy the atmosphere. Head to The Beehive Inn or The Last Drop for a budget-friendly pint of Scottish ale and a hearty meal.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — budget around £3–£5
meals.lunch: Pick up a filled roll or soup from a local bakery such as Greggs or a Scotch pie from a deli on the Royal Mile — budget £3–£6
meals.dinner: Pub meal at The Beehive Inn in Grassmarket — steak pie or fish and chips for around £10–£14 including a pint

day_by_day.notes: The Airlink 100 bus is the most budget-friendly airport transfer at £4.50 single or £7.50 return. Buy the return ticket upfront to save money. September weather in Edinburgh can be cool and rainy — pack a light waterproof jacket. Free self-guided Royal Mile walks are a great way to ease into the trip without spending on Day 1.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour — head up to the iconic fortress first thing in the morning to beat the crowds. Explore the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, St Margaret's Chapel, and sweeping views over the city. Adult entry is approximately £17–£19 with online booking (book in advance for a small discount). Spend 2–3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience — located right next to Edinburgh Castle on the Royal Mile, this award-winning attraction is the perfect follow-up. Take the barrel ride tour and guided tasting session to learn about the five whisky regions of Scotland. Entry with a dram tasting costs approximately £17–£20. A great budget-friendly introduction to Scotch without needing to visit a distillery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the independent whisky bars along the Royal Mile and nearby streets. Visit The Bow Bar on Victoria Street — one of Edinburgh's finest traditional pubs with an exceptional selection of single malts, many available as affordable drams (£4–£8 per dram). No food menu but crisps available; grab takeaway fish and chips nearby beforehand.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at accommodation or a porridge pot and coffee from a nearby café — budget £2–£5
meals.lunch: Canteen-style lunch at Elephant House Café (famous Harry Potter café) or a packed lunch from a nearby supermarket (Lidl or Co-op on South Bridge) — budget £4–£8
meals.dinner: Takeaway fish and chips from The Fryer's Delight or a chippy on Cockburn Street before your evening whisky bar visit — budget £7–£10

day_by_day.notes: Book Edinburgh Castle tickets online in advance to save a few pounds and guarantee entry. The Scotch Whisky Experience and Edinburgh Castle are directly adjacent, making this a very efficient and walkable day. The Bow Bar is cash-only — bring notes. September evenings get dark early and temperatures drop to around 10–13°C.

day_by_day.morning: Underground Vaults and Mary King's Close Tour — descend beneath the Royal Mile into the preserved 17th-century underground streets and chambers. This is one of Edinburgh's most atmospheric and historically fascinating experiences. Book in advance online; tickets cost approximately £16–£18 per adult. Tours run regularly and last about 1 hour. Highly recommended for history lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Canongate area at the lower end of the Royal Mile — visit the Museum of Edinburgh (free entry) and the Scottish Parliament building exterior. Walk through Holyrood Park to Arthur's Seat, Edinburgh's ancient volcanic peak. A moderate 45-minute hike to the summit rewards you with panoramic views of the city and beyond — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Town and explore Victoria Street, one of Edinburgh's most picturesque curved streets. Browse independent shops and enjoy the ambience. Head to Maggie Dickinson's pub on Grassmarket for live traditional Scottish music (often free on weeknights) and an affordable dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Scottish breakfast at a local café such as The Pantry or Mimi's Bakehouse on the Royal Mile — budget £6–£9
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in Holyrood Park during your Arthur's Seat hike — pick up supplies from Lidl or Co-op the night before — budget £3–£5
meals.dinner: Pub meal at Maggie Dickinson's or The White Hart Inn in Grassmarket — traditional haggis, neeps and tatties for around £10–£13

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the Arthur's Seat hike — the path can be uneven and slippery after rain. The Museum of Edinburgh is free and gives excellent context to the city's history, making it a great complement to the underground vaults tour. Mary King's Close is a private ticketed attraction — book ahead as popular time slots sell out.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street — free entry and world-class collections covering Scottish history, culture, science, and natural history. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Scottish history galleries, including Jacobite artefacts, Pictish stones, and the Lewis Chessmen. A fantastic free resource for history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget day trip or local exploration: walk up Calton Hill (free, 15-minute walk from the Royal Mile) for iconic views of the city skyline including the Scott Monument and Firth of Forth. Then visit Greyfriars Kirkyard — the historic cemetery famous for Greyfriars Bobby, covenanter graves, and rumoured Harry Potter name inspirations. Free to enter and deeply atmospheric.
day_by_day.evening: Friday evening whisky experience — visit The Scotch Malt Whisky Society on Queen Street (day membership available) or explore the whisky selection at Cadenhead's Whisky Shop and tasting room on Canongate. Many independent whisky bars offer Friday evening tasting flights. Try Whiski Rooms on North Bank Street for a curated tasting flight of 3–5 whiskies at around £15–£25.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bacon roll and coffee from a market stall at the Grassmarket morning market or a local café — budget £4–£6
meals.lunch: Self-service lunch at the National Museum of Scotland café or bring a packed lunch to eat in Greyfriars Kirkyard — budget £4–£8
meals.dinner: Budget-friendly dinner at Mosque Kitchen on Nicholson Street — legendary Edinburgh institution serving generous portions of curry and rice for £6–£9. Hugely popular with locals and students.

day_by_day.notes: Mosque Kitchen is one of Edinburgh's best-kept budget secrets — arrive early or expect a queue on Friday evenings. It is cash only. The National Museum of Scotland is free and should not be missed — allocate at least 2–3 hours. Cadenhead's Whisky Shop on Canongate is the oldest independent whisky retailer in Scotland and often offers free tastings in-store.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palace of Holyroodhouse — the official Scottish residence of the British monarch at the foot of the Royal Mile. Entry costs approximately £17–£18 and includes the historic State Apartments and the ruins of Holyrood Abbey. A rich history of Mary Queen of Scots, Bonnie Prince Charlie, and Scottish royalty. Book online in advance. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final stroll along the Royal Mile — browse the independent whisky and tartan shops for last-minute souvenirs. Pop into a local distillery shop for a miniature bottle of single malt as a budget-friendly keepsake (from £5–£10). Visit the Scottish Storytelling Centre on the Royal Mile (free entry to the building and gallery) for a final taste of Scottish culture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and a celebratory dram. Head to The Royal McGregor on the Royal Mile or Deacon Brodie's Tavern — both iconic Old Town pubs with affordable menus and a great atmosphere. Order a traditional Scottish meal and raise a glass of your favourite Scotch discovered during the trip. Finish with a walk along the illuminated Royal Mile at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a local café such as Café Andaluz or a supermarket meal deal — budget £4–£8
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a bakery or takeaway on the Royal Mile — try a Scotch pie, bridies, or a filled roll from Howie's Bakery — budget £3–£6
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Deacon Brodie's Tavern on the Royal Mile — two-course meal with a drink for approximately £18–£22 per person. Named after the real-life inspiration for Robert Louis Stevenson's Jekyll and Hyde — fitting for a history-focused trip.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time from your accommodation — store luggage at the hotel or at Edinburgh Waverley left luggage lockers (from £5) if your departure is in the evening. The Palace of Holyroodhouse may be closed to visitors when the Royal Family is in residence — check the official website before booking. Saturday on the Royal Mile is lively with street performers and market stalls, making for a memorable final afternoon.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to your Old Town hotel by taxi or Airlink 100 bus (approx. 30–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour: After settling in, join a guided afternoon walking tour along the Royal Mile. Stretching from Edinburgh Castle down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse, this 2-hour tour covers centuries of Scottish history, architecture, and storytelling — a perfect introduction to the city on your first day.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky Trail at the Canongate Pubs: Begin your Edinburgh whisky journey with a self-guided crawl through the atmospheric historic pubs of the lower Royal Mile. Start at The Tolbooth Tavern, move through The Canon's Gait, and finish at The Albanach. Sample 2–3 drams at each stop and chat with locals about their favourite expressions.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and light snack at the airport or on the transfer — no formal breakfast needed today.
meals.lunch: Deacon Brodie's Tavern on the Royal Mile — a classic mid-range Edinburgh pub serving hearty Scottish staples like cullen skink soup and smoked salmon sandwiches. Budget approx. £12–16.
meals.dinner: The Witchery by the Castle (bar menu) or Cannonball Restaurant on Castlehill — enjoy Scottish comfort food such as haggis bon bons, venison burger, or slow-cooked lamb. Budget approx. £25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 12:00 so nothing is scheduled before early afternoon. Old Town hotels are typically a 5–10 minute walk from most Royal Mile attractions. Keep luggage light for the afternoon tour — most hotels offer luggage storage if check-in isn't ready.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour: Start your day early with a visit to the iconic fortress perched on Castle Rock. Allow 2.5–3 hours to explore the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, the Great Hall, and the One O'Clock Gun. Book tickets in advance online to avoid queues. Opens at 09:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience: Conveniently located right next to Edinburgh Castle on Castlehill, this award-winning attraction is the perfect follow-up. Take the barrel-ride tour through the five whisky-producing regions of Scotland, nose and taste a flight of single malts, and browse the world's largest Scotch whisky collection. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grassmarket neighbourhood below the Castle: browse independent shops, enjoy the lively atmosphere, and end the evening at a traditional pub. The Last Drop or Maggie Dickson's are atmospheric choices with strong whisky selections and live folk music on weekday evenings.

meals.breakfast: Café Marmotte or Söderberg Bakery on Quartermile — excellent pastries, porridge, and specialty coffee. Budget approx. £7–10.
meals.lunch: The Scotch Whisky Experience includes a whisky and food pairing lunch option (book ahead), or grab a light bite at Amber Restaurant inside the attraction — Scottish cheeses, oatcakes, and charcuterie. Budget approx. £15–20.
meals.dinner: The Grain Store in the Grassmarket — a beloved Edinburgh bistro with seasonal Scottish produce, excellent wine list, and a cosy atmosphere. Try the duck confit or pan-seared sea trout. Budget approx. £28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-booking Edinburgh Castle tickets is strongly recommended — September is still peak season and queues can be long. The Scotch Whisky Experience is a 2-minute walk from the Castle exit, making this a seamlessly connected morning-to-afternoon pairing.

day_by_day.morning: Underground Vaults & Mary King's Close Tour: Descend beneath the Royal Mile into the eerily preserved 17th-century streets and chambers hidden under the South Bridge and the City Chambers. This guided 75-minute tour is fascinating for history lovers, revealing the lives of Edinburgh's past residents in one of the city's most atmospheric hidden spaces. Tours run from 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free exploration of Holyrood and Canongate: Walk the lower Royal Mile at your own pace. Visit the free Museum of Edinburgh on Canongate for local history artefacts, peek into Canongate Kirk (burial ground of Adam Smith and Robert Burns' lover), and stroll through Holyrood Park to Arthur's Seat viewpoint for panoramic city views. Allow 3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Royal Mile for an evening of culture: check if the Queen's Hall or St Giles' Cathedral has an evening concert or organ recital (common in September). Afterwards, enjoy a nightcap whisky flight at The Bow Bar on Victoria Street — one of Edinburgh's most respected whisky pubs with over 300 expressions.

meals.breakfast: The Edinburgh Larder on Blackfriars Street — a beloved neighbourhood café with locally sourced full Scottish breakfasts and homemade granola. Budget approx. £9–13.
meals.lunch: Mums Great Comfort Food on Forrest Road — iconic Edinburgh diner serving gourmet pies, sausages, and proper mac and cheese. Excellent mid-range value. Budget approx. £12–16.
meals.dinner: Ondine Restaurant on George IV Bridge — award-winning Scottish seafood restaurant with sustainably sourced langoustines, oysters, and fish. Splurge-worthy but fits mid-range with the set menu. Budget approx. £35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mary King's Close tickets should be booked in advance at realmarykingsclose.com. The afternoon Holyrood walk is free and takes advantage of Edinburgh's beautiful September light. Bring a light jacket — Arthur's Seat can be breezy even in early autumn.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Craigmillar Castle or Rosslyn Chapel: Take a short bus or taxi ride (20–30 min) to one of Edinburgh's lesser-visited historic gems. Craigmillar Castle (the 'other castle') offers atmospheric ruins with deep connections to Mary Queen of Scots and far fewer crowds than Edinburgh Castle. Alternatively, Rosslyn Chapel (featured in The Da Vinci Code) is a stunning 15th-century masterpiece of stone carvings and mystery. Allow 2–3 hours including travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Victoria Street and the Grassmarket Shopping: Return to Old Town and spend the afternoon exploring the curved, colourful Victoria Street — one of Edinburgh's most photogenic streets and the inspiration for Diagon Alley. Browse independent whisky shops (Cadenhead's Whisky Shop is a must for whisky enthusiasts), bookshops, and artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Friday Night on the Royal Mile: Edinburgh comes alive on Friday evenings. Catch a traditional Scottish ceilidh dance at The Caves or Assembly Rooms (check listings for September events), or enjoy live folk music at Sandy Bell's pub — a legendary session music venue beloved by locals. End with a dram at The Albanach's extensive whisky bar.

meals.breakfast: Peter's Yard on Quartermile — Scandinavian-inspired bakery with sourdough, crispbreads, and excellent filter coffee. Budget approx. £8–11.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café near Rosslyn/Craigmillar, or The Grassmarket Café upon return — soups, sandwiches, and daily specials. Budget approx. £10–14.
meals.dinner: The Outsider on George IV Bridge — eclectic, popular restaurant with a global-influenced Scottish menu and great views of the Castle. Known for its relaxed vibe and excellent value. Budget approx. £25–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cadenhead's Whisky Shop on Canongate is Edinburgh's oldest independent bottler and an essential stop for whisky lovers — staff are knowledgeable and will help you find a bottle to take home. Check event listings at underbelly.co.uk or visitscotland.com for Friday evening ceilidh options in September.

day_by_day.morning: Arthur's Seat Hike: If weather permits, begin your final morning with a hike up Arthur's Seat — the ancient volcano in Holyrood Park offering the best panoramic views of Edinburgh, the Firth of Forth, and the surrounding countryside. The main route takes 45–60 minutes up and is accessible from the hotel on foot (20-min walk to the park entrance). Start early to beat the weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scottish National Museum (Free Entry): Spend your last afternoon at the outstanding Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street — a world-class free museum covering Scottish history from prehistoric times through the Jacobite era, the Enlightenment, and beyond. Highlights include the Lewis Chessmen, Dolly the sheep, and extensive Jacobite artefacts. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Whisky Dinner: Celebrate your Edinburgh trip with a special farewell evening. Head to The Scotch Malt Whisky Society (SMWS) Members' Room on Queen Street for a curated tasting dinner (book ahead — day membership available for visitors), or return to a favourite Royal Mile pub for a final dram. Pick up a bottle from Royal Mile Whiskies as a souvenir.

meals.breakfast: Brew Lab Coffee on South College Street — specialty coffee roasters with excellent brunch options including avocado toast and smoked salmon bagels. Budget approx. £9–13.
meals.lunch: The National Museum of Scotland has a good café on-site (Tower Restaurant above) — try the two-course lunch menu with Scottish produce. Budget approx. £18–24.
meals.dinner: Timberyard on Lady Lawson Street — one of Edinburgh's most celebrated farm-to-table restaurants, housed in a converted Victorian warehouse. Seasonal tasting menus showcase the best of Scottish produce. Book well in advance. Budget approx. £45–60 per person for the tasting menu (a fitting farewell splurge).

day_by_day.notes: Check weather before the Arthur's Seat hike — wear sturdy shoes and bring a waterproof layer. The Scottish National Museum is free and one of the best museums in the UK, ideal for a final immersive history experience. Royal Mile Whiskies (379 High Street) is an excellent last stop for souvenir bottles and has knowledgeable staff who can recommend expressions based on your tastings throughout the week.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight BA lands at 12:00. Transfer by pre-arranged luxury private car from Edinburgh Airport to your Old Town hotel. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of Champagne or a dram of single malt provided by the concierge. Take a gentle orientation stroll along the Royal Mile to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience (14:00–15:30): Begin your Edinburgh adventure at this award-winning attraction steps from Edinburgh Castle. Embark on an immersive sensory journey through the five whisky-producing regions of Scotland, including a barrel ride and a guided nosing session. Opt for the premium 'Claive Vidiz Collection' tasting upgrade to sample rare expressions.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky Trail at the Canongate Pubs (19:00 onwards): Ease into Edinburgh's legendary pub culture with a self-guided whisky crawl along the lower Royal Mile. Begin at The Tolbooth Tavern, move through The Canongate, and finish at The Devil's Advocate — a converted Victorian pump house with an exceptional curated whisky menu of over 300 expressions.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the flight or a light bite at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: The Witchery by the Castle: Arrive in time for a late lunch (13:30) at this opulent Gothic restaurant in a 16th-century building at the top of the Royal Mile. Indulge in Scottish langoustines, hand-dived scallops, and a carefully curated wine list.
meals.dinner: Condita (20:30): An intimate, Michelin-recognised restaurant offering a refined seasonal tasting menu rooted in Scottish produce. Pre-book the chef's table experience for a personalised introduction to contemporary Scottish cuisine. Pair with their sommelier-selected wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport private transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. The Scotch Whisky Experience is a 2-minute walk from most Old Town hotels — book the 'Gold' or 'Platinum' tour tier for the premium experience. Confirm Witchery lunch reservation before arrival as it books out weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour (09:30–12:00): Beat the crowds with an early entry to Scotland's most iconic fortress perched dramatically on volcanic rock. Explore the Scottish Crown Jewels (Honours of Scotland), the Stone of Destiny, the Royal Palace, and St Margaret's Chapel — the oldest surviving building in Edinburgh. Arrange a private guided tour through the hotel concierge for an exclusive, in-depth experience with a dedicated historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour (13:30–15:30): Join a premium small-group or private guided walking tour along Edinburgh's most storied street. Your expert guide will unveil the layers of history from the medieval tenements to the Reformation, Jacobite risings, and Enlightenment. Visit key landmarks including St Giles' Cathedral, the Mercat Cross, and John Knox House.
day_by_day.evening: Underground Vaults & Mary King's Close Tour (18:00–19:30): As dusk falls, descend beneath the Royal Mile into the eerily preserved 17th-century underground streets and chambers of Mary King's Close. Book the premium evening 'Secrets' tour for a more exclusive, atmospheric experience with smaller group sizes and extended access to restricted areas.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Old Town property — opt for a full Scottish breakfast featuring Stornoway black pudding, smoked salmon, and fresh-baked morning rolls with Abernethy butter.
meals.lunch: Café St Honoré (12:30): A beloved Edinburgh institution with a refined French-Scottish bistro menu. Try the cullen skink (smoked haddock chowder) followed by braised Scottish beef cheek. Elegant yet relaxed — perfect between morning and afternoon activities.
meals.dinner: The Kitchin, Leith (20:00): Take a short taxi to Tom Kitchin's Michelin-starred flagship restaurant in the Shore district of Leith. The 'From Nature to Plate' philosophy delivers extraordinary seasonal Scottish ingredients — expect hand-dived scallops, game, and innovative desserts. Request the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Edinburgh Castle private guided tour well in advance — the castle is one of Scotland's busiest attractions. The Mary King's Close evening tour sells out quickly in September; book online at least 2 weeks ahead. Arrange a taxi or private car to Leith for dinner — approximately 15 minutes from Old Town.

day_by_day.morning: Private Whisky Masterclass (10:00–12:30): Arrange through the hotel concierge an exclusive private whisky masterclass hosted by a Scotch Whisky Association-certified Master of Whisky or a brand ambassador. Held in a private tasting room, explore the nuances of Speyside, Islay, Highland, and Lowland expressions, including rare aged single malts and limited-edition cask-strength bottlings. Learn blending techniques and create your own personalised blend to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palace of Holyroodhouse & Holyrood Park (13:30–16:30): Visit the official Scottish residence of the British monarch — a stunning royal palace at the foot of the Royal Mile. Explore the historic State Apartments, Mary Queen of Scots' chambers, and the ruined 12th-century Holyrood Abbey. Afterwards, take a scenic walk through Holyrood Park, with the option of a gentle hike up Arthur's Seat for panoramic views of the city and the Firth of Forth.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky & Cheese Pairing Experience (19:00–20:30): Return to the Scotch Whisky Experience or a specialist venue such as Cadenhead's Whisky Shop on Canongate for an intimate, guided whisky and artisan Scottish cheese pairing session. Discover how aged Speyside malts complement Isle of Mull Cheddar, or how peaty Islay drams pair with soft Crowdie cheese.

meals.breakfast: Room service or hotel dining — request a leisurely Scottish breakfast with smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, fresh fruit, and pressed juices to start a relaxed morning.
meals.lunch: Timberyard (13:00): A celebrated farm-to-table restaurant in a converted Victorian warehouse in the Grassmarket area. The Nordic-influenced Scottish menu changes daily based on foraged and locally sourced ingredients. Try the set lunch menu for exceptional value at a Michelin Bib Gourmand standard.
meals.dinner: Wedgwood the Restaurant (20:30): An elegant, intimate restaurant on the Royal Mile where chef Paul Wedgwood crafts inventive modern Scottish cuisine. Known for foraged ingredients and creative flavour combinations. Try the tasting menu and pair with selections from their impressive Scottish gin and whisky cocktail list.

day_by_day.notes: The private whisky masterclass can be arranged through specialist operators such as 'Whisky Rooms' or through the hotel's luxury concierge network. Palace of Holyroodhouse may have restricted access on certain dates when the Royal Family is in residence — verify availability in advance. Arthur's Seat hike takes approximately 45–60 minutes to the summit; wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day Excursion — The Scotch Whisky Trail: Glenkinchie Distillery (09:30–13:00): Arrange a private chauffeured day trip (approximately 25 minutes from Edinburgh) to Glenkinchie — the 'Edinburgh Malt' and one of Scotland's few remaining Lowland distilleries. Book the premium 'Distiller's Edition' tour for exclusive access to the warehouses, a cask sample directly from the barrel, and a guided tasting of rare expressions not available to the general public.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rosslyn Chapel & Scottish Countryside (13:30–16:30): Continue your chauffeured excursion to the breathtaking Rosslyn Chapel in Midlothian (made famous by The Da Vinci Code). Marvel at the extraordinary medieval stone carvings, the Apprentice Pillar, and the richly decorated interior. Stroll through the scenic Roslin Glen Country Park before returning to Edinburgh in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: New Town Exploration & Gin Cocktail Bar (18:00–20:00): Return refreshed and explore Edinburgh's elegant Georgian New Town. Visit the Scottish National Portrait Gallery (open until 17:00) before settling into heads & Tales or The Bon Vivant — sophisticated cocktail bars celebrating Scottish spirits, including Edinburgh Gin expressions and whisky-forward cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — a full leisurely Scottish breakfast before your early departure for the day excursion.
meals.lunch: The Original Rosslyn Inn (13:00, Roslin Village): A charming, historic inn adjacent to Rosslyn Chapel serving hearty Scottish lunches — Scotch broth, venison pie, and local cheeses. A perfectly atmospheric midday stop between distillery and chapel.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Martin Wishart, Leith (20:30): The pinnacle of Edinburgh fine dining — Martin Wishart's eponymous Michelin-starred restaurant in Leith is widely regarded as one of the finest in Scotland. An extraordinary French-influenced tasting menu showcasing the very best of Scottish seasonal produce. An essential reservation for any luxury Edinburgh visit — book months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private chauffeured vehicle for the full day through the hotel concierge — a knowledgeable driver-guide familiar with distillery routes is ideal. Glenkinchie premium tours must be booked directly with the distillery well in advance. Restaurant Martin Wishart is among Edinburgh's most sought-after tables — confirm reservation before departure from home.

day_by_day.morning: Scottish National Museum (10:00–12:00): Spend your final morning at the magnificent Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street — free entry and world-class. Explore the Scottish History and Archaeology galleries, the Jacobite collection, and the extraordinary Lewis Chessmen on display. A deeply enriching final immersion into Scottish history, culture, and identity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Bespoke Whisky Shopping & Farewell Dram (13:00–15:30): Dedicate your final afternoon to curating your personal whisky collection. Visit Cadenhead's Whisky Shop (the oldest independent bottler in Scotland, established 1842) on Canongate for rare, cask-strength single cask bottlings. Then browse Royal Mile Whiskies for an extraordinary selection of aged and rare expressions. Conclude with a farewell dram at The Scotch Malt Whisky Society members' bar on Queen Street — arrange temporary guest access through the hotel concierge for a truly exclusive send-off.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Preparation (19:00): A relaxed, celebratory final dinner before preparing for onward travel. Return to your hotel for a final evening in Old Town Edinburgh.

meals.breakfast: A special farewell breakfast at The Colonnades at The Signet Library or your hotel's finest breakfast offering — smoked salmon, eggs Royale, pastries, fresh fruit, and a glass of Champagne to mark the end of a remarkable trip.
meals.lunch: The Café Royal (13:00): An Edinburgh institution since 1863, housed in a stunning Victorian interior with ornate tiled portraits of famous inventors. The oyster bar and seafood menu are exceptional — try a dozen Loch Fyne oysters, dressed Cromer crab, and a glass of Chablis Premier Cru.
meals.dinner: Number One at The Balmoral Hotel (19:30): End your Edinburgh journey in the grandest style at Number One — the Michelin-starred restaurant within the iconic Balmoral Hotel on Princes Street. An exquisite modern Scottish tasting menu in a sumptuous Art Deco dining room. Request the whisky trolley to conclude your meal with a rare aged dram — the perfect final toast to an unforgettable Edinburgh experience.

day_by_day.notes: Pack whisky purchases carefully — specialist shops such as Cadenhead's and Royal Mile Whiskies offer secure packaging and international shipping if bottles exceed airline carry-on limits. The Scotch Malt Whisky Society guest access should be arranged 24–48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge. Arrange a private airport transfer for your departure — confirm timing with the hotel the evening before.
